02 / Problem statement

The official wording, reflowed for the screen

Five pages, five problems, one recommendation letter. Paragraph breaks and hyphenation were normalized; the wording is unchanged.

2026 Asia and Pacific Mathematical Contest in Modeling · Problem A

Flood Disaster Assessment and Emergency Rescue Optimization

Based on Image Recognition

Flood disasters are among the major natural disasters threatening people's lives and property. Flooding caused by heavy rainfall can inundate residential areas, disrupt transportation networks, and affect the operation of public facilities within a short period of time, posing severe challenges to population evacuation, medical assistance, and the transportation of relief supplies. After a disaster occurs, rapidly assessing disaster conditions, accurately identifying affected areas, scientifically evaluating rescue needs, and developing effective rescue plans under time and resource constraints are important challenges in disaster prevention, mitigation, and emergency management. Figure 1 presents satellite images of the Dongting Lake dike breach in Huarong County, Yueyang City, Hunan Province, before and after the disaster. Before the disaster, the area consisted of green farmland, villages, and normal waterways. After the disaster, large areas of farmland and villages were inundated by floodwaters, resulting in extensive newly inundated areas.

Timely acquisition of disaster information is a prerequisite for effective rescue operations. However, flood disasters are characterized by sudden occurrence, extensive impacts, and significant spatial variations. Traditional ground surveys are often constrained by road disruptions, damaged communication infrastructure, and challenging on-site conditions, making it difficult to obtain timely and comprehensive information about affected areas. Particularly during the initial stages of emergency rescue, the conflict between incomplete information and the need for timely decision-making becomes especially pronounced. With the development of satellite remote sensing, intelligent image recognition, and geographic information technologies, multi-source imagery has provided new technical approaches for rapid disaster detection. Optical imagery can directly reveal surface characteristics, while Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery offers certain advantages in all-day and all-weather observation and can provide important supplementary information under cloudy and rainy conditions. Through image preprocessing, feature extraction, and multi-source information fusion, flood-inundated areas can be identified and the spatial distribution of disaster impacts can be analyzed, providing data support for rapid disaster assessment. Therefore, the key challenges lie in reliably identifying disaster conditions despite differences among multi-source data and incomplete information, translating inundation information into regional disaster assessment results, and using these results to support emergency rescue decision-making. These challenges present a mathematical modeling problem of significant practical importance.

Modeling requirements

Please develop mathematical models for the specified study area and flood event to address the following problems. Except for Problem 1, relevant imagery and reference data required for model training and validation may be independently obtained through Copernicus Browser or other publicly available platforms. Geographic information, statistical data, and disaster records may also be supplemented as needed. During the modeling process, the data sources, acquisition times, spatial coverage, and processing methods should be clearly specified. When data are insufficient, reasonable assumptions may be made. However, assumed parameters must be distinguished from actual observational data, and their impacts on the model results should be analyzed.

P1P2P3P4P5
Problem 1 · 01

Remote Sensing Image Processing and Identification of Flood-Inundated Areas

Accurate identification of flood-inundated areas is an important foundation for disaster monitoring and rescue decision-making. Using the pre-disaster optical imagery, post-disaster SAR imagery, and corresponding label information provided in Attachment 1, perform the necessary image preprocessing and develop a model for identifying flood-inundated areas. Evaluate the recognition performance of the model using independent samples. In addition to pixel-level recognition accuracy, particular emphasis should be placed on the estimation error of newly inundated area, relative area error, and the degree of spatial overlap between inundated regions. Analyze how false positives and false negatives under different land-cover conditions affect the estimation of newly inundated area, and investigate the key factors influencing the accuracy of flood-inundated area identification.

Problem 2 · 02

Multi-Source Information Fusion and Improvement of the Flood-Inundated Area Identification Model

Under complex disaster conditions, a single type of imagery and recognition method may be insufficient to accurately characterize flood inundation. For cases in Problem 1 where recognition performance is poor or uncertainty is relatively high, investigate multi-source information fusion and model improvement methods. With the primary objectives of improving the accuracy of newly inundated area estimation and reducing area estimation errors, develop a more accurate and reliable model for identifying newly inundated areas caused by flooding. On this basis, establish a flood inundation intensity classification method using the newly inundated area and its proportion of the total area of the study region as the core indicators. Clearly define the area or proportion thresholds corresponding to different intensity levels, distinguish among general, relatively strong, strong, and extremely strong flood inundation conditions, and analyze the effects of area identification errors and their uncertainties on the classification results.

Problem 3 · 03

Identification of Newly Inundated Areas and Flood Inundation Intensity Analysis in Hengzhou City, Guangxi

Apply the model developed in Problem 2 to the flooding process occurring around July 6, 2026, in Hengzhou City, Guangxi, to examine the applicability of the model in a real disaster scenario. Independently determine an appropriate study area and select representative imagery acquired before and during the flood event. Identify pre-existing water bodies and newly inundated areas caused by flooding, quantitatively calculate the newly inundated area, the net increase in inundated area, and the proportion of newly inundated area, and present the spatial distribution of the newly inundated areas.

Problem 4 · 04

Regional Flood Disaster Assessment Based on Newly Inundated Areas

The extent and spatial distribution of newly inundated areas can reflect the geographic scope of disaster impacts. However, the severity of disaster impacts across different regions is also influenced by factors such as population distribution, infrastructure, and rescue conditions. Based on the newly inundated areas identified in Problem 3, obtain publicly available data on population, buildings, roads, hospitals, shelters, terrain, and other relevant factors as needed. Independently determine appropriate spatial assessment units and establish a comprehensive regional disaster assessment model that takes newly inundated area, inundation proportion, and flood inundation intensity as the core indicators, while also considering the exposure of populations and critical facilities.

Problem 5 · 05

Emergency Rescue Optimization and Management Recommendations Driven by Flood Disaster Information

The ultimate value of disaster identification lies in enabling limited rescue resources to serve areas and populations in urgent need of assistance in a more timely and targeted manner. Based on the preceding disaster identification and assessment results, select one specific task for optimization from rescue site selection, emergency supply allocation, rescue transportation route planning, or resident evacuation arrangements. Alternatively, a rescue task with a clearly defined practical application context may be proposed independently. Clearly specify the decision-making time point, optimization objectives, demand estimation methods, available resources, and constraints, and establish a corresponding optimization model. The model should ensure that the results of image recognition and disaster assessment are directly incorporated into rescue decision-making, demonstrating an effective connection between disaster monitoring and resource scheduling. Model parameters may be obtained from publicly available sources.

Recommendation letter

Finally, write a letter of recommendations to the local emergency management authorities, proposing actionable measures regarding flood remote sensing monitoring, disaster information updates, and the scientific allocation of rescue resources. The letter should also explain the implementation conditions and scope of applicability of the proposed measures.

08 / Notes

What was changed, and what was not

A short provenance note so the preview is not mistaken for the raw archive.

01

Source and sizes

Built from the three uploaded zips. Byte counts come from the ZIP central directory; outer sizes from the filesystem. Uncompressed totals are the sum of the raster members.

02

Problem text

Extracted from the 5-page PDF, reflowed by paragraph, with line-end hyphenation repaired. The facsimile pages are rendered at 1.7× for verification.

03

Raster previews

Labels are colorized 0/1 masks. SAR is grayscale with per-patch autocontrast. Optical is a BGR→RGB natural-color composite from the first three channels with mild brightness/contrast; channel 4 is omitted.

04

Contact sheets

Each sheet contains all 1,000 patches of one layer as 48 px thumbnails, 40 per row, in suffix order 1001→2000. They are navigation aids, not substitutes for the TIFFs.

05

Privacy

The public page contains no team member names, school or advisor. PDF metadata is not displayed. Only the contest identity, problem title and team-neutral archive facts are shown.

06

Scope

This is a navigable reading edition, not an official publication. The official problem wording remains the property of the contest organizers.

Single-file guarantee: all CSS, JavaScript and preview imagery are inline in this HTML document. There are no external fonts, CDNs, image files or JSON requests. The raw TIFFs remain in the source archives and are deliberately not base64-embedded.
